recall_prompt: Say how you would find the magnitude of a cross product.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find a×b
steps.margin_note: First mark. Straight determinant. Watch the double negatives — (−1)(−5) is +5, not −5.

recall.must_convey: That a×b is computed as a determinant, giving 8i + 11j − 5k.
accept: expand the determinant to get eight i plus eleven j minus five k
take the cross product of a and b
a cross b is eight i plus eleven j minus five k
determinant expand cheste eight i plus eleven j minus five k

steps.why: The magnitude cannot be found without the vector first — there is no shortcut from the components of a and b directly.
common_mistakes: Sign slip on a product of two negatives.
Forgetting the minus in front of the j term.

steps.label: Take the magnitude
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Square, add, root. 210 has no square factor, so the surd is the final answer.

accept: square the components and add to get two hundred ten so the magnitude is root two ten
the modulus is root two hundred and ten
sixty four plus one twenty one plus twenty five is two ten
the magnitude is root two ten

steps.why: Every term in a magnitude is a square, so the negative component contributes +25. A negative under the root would mean an arithmetic slip.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to square the negative and subtracting 5.
Trying to simplify √210, which has no square factor.
